4.text: again becomes a dog, and drags away the woman as dogs usually do. The

5.text: body of the woman is torn to pieces, and only a small part of the pelvis is

6.text: brought to the house of the master of the “spell.” The dog, after coming

7.text: home, vanishes. The details about the dog-man cohabiting with a woman,

8.text: after the manner of dogs, occurs also in the tales of the American Eskimo,²

9.text: but the dog is not represented as a materialized “spell.”

10.text: In the collection of Chukchee sketches, the materialized “spell” is represented

11.text: by several drawings. Now it is a half-bodied seal sent by a mischievous shaman

12.text: to frighten a seal-hunter; again it has the form

13.text: of two bears who have caught a woman “doomed

14.text: to anger,” and are torturing her, tossing her body

15.text: to and fro between themselves like a ball (Fig. 296).

16.text: The malicious incantations are believed to

17.text: work sometimes in the same way as do the

18.text: materialized “spells;” that is, by inducing the

19.text: person “doomed to anger” to meet the harm in a quasi-natural way. For instance,

20.text: while travelling on the Wolverene River, I met a man by the name of Peˊtki,

21.text: who formerly was one of the fleetest runners in the whole neighborhood. His

22.text: rivals, desirous that his speed should be impaired, sent an incantation to him

23.text: by which he was induced, while in his own sleeping-room, to sit down on a

24.text: bare knife, and in such a manner that half of the blade entered his thigh.

25.text: When I saw him, he was still suffering from the wound, and it was impossible

28.text: The people are excessively afraid of all kinds of “spells” and harmful

29.text: incantations; but, on the other hand, they often wish to retaliate on the

30.text: suspected wrong-doer. Even a great shaman of the mischievous kind is not

31.text: safe from the revenge of his neighbors, who by common consent may cause

32.text: his death.³ Thus, in the tale of “The Scabby Shaman,” the people wronged

33.text: by young Rɪˊntew make complaint to his father, and then the whole village

34.text: plans the destruction of the young shaman.

35.text: Even in modern times, when harm of an unexpected character is ascribed

36.text: to the pernicious influence of an unfriendly neighbor, the latter runs the risk

37.text: of paying for the suspected witchcraft with his life. Thus, in the year 1896,
